OpenAI has updated the recently redesigned ChatGPT Mac app, making it easier for users to once again access their conversations. Here's what you need to know.

OpenAI addresses major complaints after confusing ChatGPT Mac app redesign

Last Thursday, OpenAI rolled out an entirely new ChatGPT Mac app that combined ChatGPT, Codex, and the newly announced Work agent into one, while renaming the old app to ChatGPT Classic.

The change proved controversial for two main reasons: first, the new app replaced the original native Mac client with a much larger app based on the Electron framework. Second, the interface design was confusing, featuring a prominent dropdown for switching between Codex and Work, while the standard Chat experience was demoted to an inconspicuous button that opened a floating window with no access to users' existing conversations or Projects.

Following the update, users immediately voiced frustrations about the confusing changes on OpenAI's community forums and X. The next day, Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, who has been leading OpenAI's efforts to merge ChatGPT and Codex into a unified "super app," acknowledged the criticism and committed to restoring conversations and Projects to the sidebar, clarifying the distinction between ChatGPT Work and Codex, and addressing other usability issues.

OpenAI has now updated the new ChatGPT app to address some of those complaints, most notably the inability to directly access conversations. Users can now switch between Chat and Work via a prominent toggle at the top of the window, while the sidebar dropdown lets users choose between regular ChatGPT and Codex.

9to5Mac's take

Although the ChatGPT app's interface remains confusing, users who simply want to use ChatGPT can now once again use the chatbot like before.

Still, this puzzling rollout — which demoted ChatGPT to a second-class citizen behind Work and Codex, paired with the switch to Electron — gives the impression that OpenAI is more focused on competing with Anthropic than delivering a polished experience for users. Luckily, ChatGPT Classic still exists, and as long as it's available, there's still room to switch back.
